facts.value: Mastering keyboarding is much like playing the piano. Each finger has a designated set of keys to press, and training them to move effortlessly builds muscle memory. Just as a pianist practices scales and finger placement, a typist learns key distribution through structured exercises. Our keyboarding program introduces new keys gradually, starting with isolated practice before incorporating them into small words using the letters learned so far. As you progress, exercises expand to longer words, full sentences, practice paragraphs and test text drills. Through repetition and continuous practice, you develop speed, accuracy, and fluency — much like a musician mastering their instrument.

facts.value: The difference is dramatic — not just in speed, but in comfort and control. Using all fingers unlocks your full potential and transforms keyboarding into a smooth, almost effortless skill.
